tasks.short: Answer calls, provide routine information, record messages and connect callers to the right person.

steps.what: Answer the call and establish the caller's needs.
Find contact details or approved information for the caller's request.
Explain the answer, check understanding and handle questions.
Record a message and send it to the requested recipient when needed.
Transfer the caller when a suitable recipient is available.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable directory and approved answer cards in the {DOCS}, using only permitted directory fields from the {HCM}. Configure message forms and transfer shortcuts around the {TELEPHONY}, with internal messages delivered through the {EMAIL}. The assistant handles the conversation and selects what information to disclose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact lists and answer documents were scattered. Keeping them current required cooperation across departments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, forms and telephone controls cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can make small connectors cheaper to build; no new model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising urgency, protecting private information and finding someone who will take an unusual call.
tasks.human_edge: Hear distress, understand an unclear request and make the caller feel heard.

ambition.what: A callback service for unanswered calls, with a named recipient and due time.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less searching and message copying. The assistant can prioritise callback follow-up within agreed service rules; authority to disclose information does not expand.

reach.task: Review repeated routing failures and adjust reception coverage.
reach.learn: Service measures, call categories and staffing constraints.

evidence.claim: Directory search, structured message forms and telephone shortcuts can reduce handling effort without a model.
GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose limitation and retention for caller and employee information.

assumptions: This is a human reception service, with no automatic caller conversation or recording.
The directory exposes approved business contact fields, not unrestricted employee records.
Messages and transfers are alternative branches; shares represent their average contribution across calls.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether the {TELEPHONY} supports message forms, directory lookup and transfer shortcuts.
Who maintains approved answers and contact availability.
Actual call mix, handling time and frequency of sensitive inquiries.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered from a short, approved reference?
Can existing configuration supply the directory without a custom connector?
new_work: Update contact destinations and approved answers.
Follow up overdue callbacks and failed transfers.
Check access permissions and message retention.

tasks.short: Welcome visitors, understand their needs, contact hosts and give appropriate directions or information.

steps.what: Welcome the visitor and establish their purpose and intended host.
Check the appointment, host details and relevant visitor instructions.
Tell the host that the visitor has arrived.
Confirm whether to receive the visitor or arrange another response.
Give directions, explain the response or help the visitor with remaining questions.

tasks.design: Configure an arrival form in the {WORKFLOW} that retrieves permitted visit details from the {CALENDAR} and instructions from the {DOCS}. It notifies the host through the {CHAT} and records their response before reception directs the visitor onwards. Reception keeps the welcome and handles unexpected needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reception depended on calendar access, separate instructions and informal messages to hosts.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, calendar permissions and notification flows are established capabilities. Small integrations can now be built and adjusted at lower development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected visitors, absent hosts, language barriers and situations requiring discretion.
tasks.human_edge: Make visitors comfortable and adapt assistance to their circumstances.

ambition.what: A pre-arrival assistance service for visitors who request accessibility support.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time locating hosts and chasing replies. They can coordinate requested visitor assistance within agreed limits; hosts retain decisions about receiving visitors.

reach.task: Arrange accessible routes and visitor assistance.
reach.learn: Building access, accessibility arrangements and escalation contacts.

evidence.claim: Calendar lookup, arrival notifications and explicit host responses can use deterministic workflow configuration.
Visitor records need proportionate collection, restricted access and defined retention under GDPR.

assumptions: This task primarily covers physical reception; telephone handling is described in the separate call task.
Reception checks appointments without seeing unrelated calendar content.
Shares cover active handling across participants and exclude visitor waiting time.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Assistance requests record practical arrangements rather than unnecessary health details.
unknowns: Whether visit appointments are available to reception in the {CALENDAR}.
Current host approval and building access arrangements.
Languages, visitor volumes and accessibility needs.
Applicable national rules and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can a calendar-derived visit list replace repeated appointment searches?
Which host responses and fallback contacts should the arrival form offer?
new_work: Maintain host fallback contacts and visitor instructions.
Handle unmatched appointments and unanswered notifications.
Review visitor record retention and coordinate requested assistance.

tasks.short: Create and update administrative records, check their accuracy and resolve missing or conflicting information.

steps.what: Receive source records and identify the requested additions or changes.
Compare requested changes with existing entries in the administrative records application.
Ask the record owner to resolve missing fields or conflicting information.
Create or amend entries and supporting fields in the administrative records application.
Check saved entries against sources and correct errors in the administrative records application.

tasks.design: Replace emailed structured changes with validated forms in the {WORKFLOW}, and connect them to the {OTHER} administrative records application. Deterministic checks enforce field rules, detect duplicates and apply authorised updates with a change log. A review screen shows rejected updates and samples of accepted records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different teams supplied different formats. Field ownership, duplicate rules and reliable write access were often unclear.
tasks.enabler_now: Form validation, import routines and change logs are established technology. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and validation screens.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing the source of truth, resolving conflicting records and migrating legacy data.
tasks.human_edge: Determine what an ambiguous record means and obtain a reliable answer from its owner.

ambition.what: A pre-event contact-data check for project coordinators.

tasks.altitude: Routine rekeying largely disappears, leaving an exception queue and periodic quality checks. The assistant gains authority to correct agreed low-risk field errors; disputed facts and schema changes still need the record owner's decision.

reach.task: Identify recurring data defects that delay administrative processes.
reach.learn: Field definitions, source ownership and basic data-quality analysis.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, field validation, duplicate checks and record updates can be implemented without model inference.
GDPR requires personal records to be accurate, appropriately secured and retained for a defined purpose.

assumptions: Most inputs are structured, consistent with the supplied prior.
Database creation usually means creating administrative lists, fields and records rather than infrastructure administration.
Automatic writes cover authorised, reversible updates that pass explicit rules.
New schemas, sensitive changes and ambiguous matches remain blocked for owner approval.
The form removes the need to interpret free-text change requests in the automatic path.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: The category, access controls and import interfaces of the {OTHER} administrative records application.
Which fields the assistant may create or amend.
Whether upstream records can eliminate duplicate entry entirely.
Actual exception rates, duplicate rates and record sensitivity.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which repeated entries can be eliminated by using the authoritative record directly?
Can existing forms and import configuration cover the required validations?
Which updates require approval before writing rather than a later quality check?
new_work: Resolve rejected updates and ambiguous duplicate matches.
Maintain field mappings, validation rules and authorised write scopes.
Sample accepted records and investigate recurring defects.
Check failed imports and reconcile change logs.

tasks.short: Use office applications to turn requests and source information into checked, usable administrative documents.

steps.what: Read the request and identify the required document, audience and deadline.
Find the source documents, approved template and relevant administrative records.
Write and format the requested letter, memo or administrative report.

loop.input: Document brief, approved template and permission-filtered source pack.
loop.output: Document draft with source references and unresolved fields marked.
loop.check: Validate required sections and exact structured fields; require sources for factual claims and human review.
loop.stop: One draft per request, with fixed input and output limits. Failed validation returns the template and sources for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Field merging handles standard sections, but narrative memos need wording from varied source text.

steps.what: Check facts, wording, recipients and layout; approve or return the draft.
Save the approved version in the correct folder with its reference details.

tasks.design: A request form in the {WORKFLOW} collects document requirements, while a connector retrieves approved templates and permitted records from the {DOCS} and the {OTHER} administrative records application. A deterministic generator fills standard sections, with one bounded drafting loop only for narrative text. After the assistant approves the document, the {WORKFLOW} files the approved version in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived in inconsistent formats, and staff copied facts between records and documents. Narrative wording did not fit fixed templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Template generation and record retrieval are established capabilities. Bounded drafting can assist with narrative sections, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting the parts.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete briefs, contradictory sources, document layout and wording that could create an unintended commitment.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the audience, recognise misleading wording and decide when the requester must clarify the substance.

ambition.what: A project-start briefing pack for small internal projects.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time locating sources and formatting drafts, and more time checking meaning and handling unclear requests. They can assemble briefing packs from approved sources; authority to make commitments does not increase.

reach.task: Prepare a project-start briefing with scope, contacts and open questions.
reach.learn: Project scope, document dependencies and issue tracking.

evidence.claim: Templates fed by structured records can generate standard document sections without model inference.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting time savings, hallucinations and no evidence of higher productivity overall.
The EU AI Act requires AI literacy; ordinary drafting is not itself an Annex III employment use.
GDPR still applies to personal information in source packs and generated documents.

assumptions: This broad computer-use task is illustrated through document preparation, not counted as additional time over database work.
Many document sections use fixed templates; only narrative sections need the drafting loop.
Sources are permission-filtered before drafting, and model processing follows agreed data-handling arrangements.
The assistant may approve routine internal documents; commitments and restricted documents follow existing approval routes.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not transferred from the cited case.
Review time is retained in full because generated wording may need substantive correction.
unknowns: The actual mix of documents, database work and other application use.
Available templates and authoritative source locations.
The category and retrieval interfaces of the {OTHER} administrative records application.
Which documents require a manager's approval or external delivery.
Approved model processing, retention and access arrangements.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which document families can use template generation alone?
Does narrative drafting reduce total preparation time after review and corrections?
Can source references and unresolved fields be checked reliably before review?
new_work: Review generated wording, facts and unresolved fields.
Maintain templates, source mappings and drafting instructions.
Handle retrieval failures and contradictory source material.
Maintain representative quality checks and staff AI literacy.

role.altitude: The role shifts towards welcoming people, resolving unclear requests and checking administrative outputs. Routine lookup, rekeying and formatting shrink; broader decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Administrative services manager: use routing and callback evidence to improve reception coverage.
Facilities manager: coordinate visitor assistance and accessible routes.
Management analyst: investigate recurring administrative data defects.
Project management specialist: assemble project-start briefings from approved sources.
skills_to_grow: Structured intake and practical workflow configuration.
Data validation, record ownership and exception handling.
Document review, source checking and AI literacy.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a small administrative support service combining reliable callbacks, accessible visitor preparation, contact-data checks and project-start briefing packs, with clear authority limits and named escalation contacts.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
